neighbours.label: Fires on the possessive determiner (our, their, his, nos, allen) that introduces a group of people who stand with or support someone, such as sponsors, partners, families, followers or flatterers, predicting a people noun; quiet on the same determiners before objects or places.
fire: The festival would not exist without the help of our generous donors and volunteers.
Wir bedanken uns herzlich bei unseren Partnern und Unterstützern.
Nous tenons à remercier tous nos mécènes et nos amis.
The emperor trusted his courtiers more than his own generals.
Patients and their caregivers deserve clear information.
The museum honored its patrons at a dinner in the main hall.
We are grateful to all our supporters who made this season possible.
The senator thanked her constituents and allies after the vote.
quiet: The festival would not exist without the size of our big parking field.
Wir bedanken uns herzlich für das schöne Wetter am Wochenende.
Nous tenons à repeindre toutes nos fenêtres et nos portes.
The emperor trusted his maps more than his own memory of the roads.
Patients and their medical charts are moved to the new wing.
The museum cleaned its floors before the dinner in the main hall.
We are grateful that all our equipment arrived in time this season.
The senator parked her car and walked to the vote.

predictions: 6/8 fire >= 0.25 (probes 0.27-0.73: 'thank our sponsors' 0.67, 'nos partenaires' 0.73, 'allen Personen' 0.64, 'his flatterers' 0.55, 'and their families' 0.27); near misses < 0.1 ('our roof' 0.004, 'thank you' 0.04).
notes: Probes (fraction of max 174): thanks to sponsors/partners in English, French and German 0.64-0.73; 'his flatterers' 0.55; 'its benefactors' 0.31; 'their families' 0.27; 'thank you for reading' 0.04; 'our roof' 0.004. The + pole suppresses 'friends', so the - pole leans toward predicting supporter/friend nouns.
